prompts.title: Forma reciente
prompts.prompt:
VERTICAL 9:16 · ~10 s · goat-lab charcoal #101412 background, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf accents. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles; keep all graphics above that band.

EDITORIAL VARIANT (0–4.5 s): kinetic typography on charcoal. Spanish team names as stacked word-blocks: 'RED BULL SALZBURG' in lime and 'AC MILAN' in slate, each set in a heavy condensed sans, weight 800, tracking slightly negative. Three rhythmic beats: each beat pops a Spanish result word — 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES', 'DERROTAS' — center-frame for a third of a second, scaling from 1.35 to 1.0 with a sharp ease-out and a 2-frame lime underline swipe. Team badges are omitted; keep it typographic. The beat grid locks to the narrator cadence. Exit with a hard transition (cut on the downbeat) into the statistical variant.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (4.5–10 s): grouped count bars, shared zero baseline anchored at 1520 px from top, chart width 820 px. Three category groups along the horizontal axis labelled in Spanish: 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES', 'DERROTAS'. Inside each group two vertical bars: Salzburg (lime) and Milan (slate), unit 'partidos', integer ticks 0–3 with 1-partido gridlines in low-opacity warm white. Reference values exactly: Salzburg {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}; Milan {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Entry: axis draws left-to-right in 0.4 s, then bars grow upward from the baseline with a 0.08 s stagger, ease-out cubic, count-up numerals in warm white above each bar. Main comparison: the tallest pair in each group is emphasized with a 2 px lime outline and a subtle 6 px lift. Labels in Spanish use unit 'partidos' spelled under the axis. Source and sample annotation at 48 px warm white at 70 opacity, above the subtitle band: 'Últimos {{home.n}} partidos (muestra de {{away.n}}) · Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Camera: gentle 1.0→1.03 push during bar growth, then locked. Exit: bars retract to baseline in 0.3 s and the frame wipes upward into the next scene.

prompts.title: Balance de goles
prompts.prompt:
VERTICAL 9:16 · ~9 s · charcoal #101412 canvas, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for Salzburg, slate #8ca6bf for Milan. Lower quarter permanently reserved for yellow subtitles.

EDITORIAL VARIANT (0–4 s): illustrative football pitch drawn in thin warm-white line work, top-down, occupying the upper two thirds, with a subtle lime centre-circle glow. Two stylised ball paths animate: a lime dashed arc curving from the left touchline into the goal area, and a mirrored slate arc. A small warm-white ball travels each arc with motion blur, leaving a fading trail. Spanish generic headings only: 'GOLES A FAVOR' and 'GOLES RECIBIDOS' appear as small corner labels in condensed uppercase. No statistical axes, no sample claims, no invented match events — pure illustrative energy. Entry: pitch lines stroke on in 0.5 s; exit: a transition wipe along the goal line into the statistical variant.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (4–9 s): paired horizontal bars, shared scale max = highest value among {{home.gf}}, {{home.ga}}, {{away.gf}}, {{away.ga}}, drawn from a common left origin at 180 px so all four bars share one unit ('goles'). Row 1: Salzburg goles a favor {{home.gf}} (lime) and goles recibidos {{home.ga}} (lime at 45 opacity outline); row 2: Milan goles a favor {{away.gf}} (slate) and goles recibidos {{away.ga}} (slate at 45 opacity). Each bar carries a Spanish label to its left in 34 px warm white and a unit suffix 'goles' after the count-up numeral. Football context: a tiny line-ball icon sits beside the 'goles a favor' labels. Entry: bars slide in from origin over 0.6 s with ease-out and stagger 0.07 s. Main comparison: the paired gap between scored and conceded is highlighted with a thin bracket and a Spanish micro-caption 'DIFERENCIA'. Emphasis: the largest bar gets a 3 px warm-white outline pulse once. Source and sample annotation in Spanish at 46 px: 'Muestra: últimos {{home.n}} partidos · Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Camera: a slow 40 px vertical drift between rows, then lock. Exit: bars fade and the frame slides left into the next scene via transition.

prompts.title: Arcos en cero
prompts.prompt:
VERTICAL 9:16 · ~8 s · charcoal #101412 base, warm white #edf0e6 typography, lime #c5ed74 for Salzburg, slate #8ca6bf for Milan. Lower quarter kept clear for permanent yellow subtitles.

EDITORIAL VARIANT (0–3.5 s): defensive energy — a stylised shield built from two overlapping angular planes, one lime (Salzburg) one slate (Milan), meeting at a warm-white seam in the centre of the frame. The shield assembles from six flying polygon fragments with a 0.4 s stagger and a firm ease-out, then breathes with a subtle 1.0→1.015 scale loop. Impact rings ripple outward on each beat, like blocked shots, drawn as thin warm-white arcs. Spanish generic heading 'DEFENSA' in condensed uppercase at the top third. No axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Entry: fragments converge from outside the 9:16 frame; exit via a transition (shutter close on the shield seam) into the statistical variant.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (3.5–8 s): two vertical count bars on a shared zero baseline at 1560 px, unit 'partidos', ticks 0–3. Bar A lime, Spanish label 'RED BULL SALZBURG · ARCOS EN CERO', value {{home.clean}}; Bar B slate, Spanish label 'AC MILAN · ARCOS EN CERO', value {{away.clean}}. Counts stay counts — do NOT convert into rates or ratios. Beneath each bar, in warm white at 60 opacity, an attached sample line in Spanish: 'Muestra: últimos {{home.n}} partidos' and 'Muestra: últimos {{away.n}} partidos' respectively, so the unequal-looking bars are read against their samples. Entry: baseline strokes in 0.3 s, bars grow over 0.7 s with ease-out cubic, numerals count up in 56 px warm white. Main comparison: the taller bar receives a 3 px lime outline and a one-time vertical lift of 10 px. Source annotation at 46 px above the subtitle band: 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Camera: locked, with a single 1.02 push on the emphasis beat. Exit: bars retract downward and the frame cross-fades into the next scene by transition.

prompts.title: Cruces previos
prompts.prompt:
VERTICAL 9:16 · ~8 s · charcoal #101412 background, warm white #edf0e6 text, lime #c5ed74 (Salzburg) versus slate #8ca6bf (Milan). Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles.

EDITORIAL VARIANT (0–3.5 s): a visual duel. The frame splits vertically by a warm-white seam; the left half tints lime with the Spanish word 'RED BULL SALZBURG' rotated 90 degrees in heavy condensed type, the right half tints slate with 'AC MILAN'. On two beats the halves lunge toward the seam by 40 px and recoil, with a flash of warm-white sparks along the seam and a subtle screen shake of 6 px. Between lunges, the word 'DUELO' in condensed uppercase scales from 1.2 to 1.0 with a snap. Purely editorial — no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Entry: seam draws top-to-bottom in 0.3 s; exit via a transition (seam expands to full frame and wipes) into the statistical variant.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (3.5–8 s): a single horizontal stacked count bar spanning 780 px, shared zero at the left origin, unit 'partidos', total segment length equals {{h2h.total}}. Segments in Spanish order: 'SALZBURG · VICTORIAS' {{h2h.homeWins}} in lime, 'EMPATES' {{h2h.draws}} in warm white at 30 opacity, 'AC MILAN · VICTORIAS' {{h2h.awayWins}} in slate. Where a segment equals zero, show a thin outlined placeholder with the Spanish label 'SIN VICTORIAS' rather than an invisible segment, so the reader sees an empty count, not missing data. Entry: segments grow from the shared origin with 0.1 s stagger and ease-out. Numerals count up above each segment with unit 'partidos'. Main comparison: the Milan segment is emphasized with a 3 px warm-white outline and a 8 px lift. Historical data is not a forecast — the Spanish micro-caption 'DATOS HISTÓRICOS' sits permanently under the axis. Source and sample annotation at 46 px: 'Cruces previos · Muestra: {{h2h.total}} partidos · Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Camera locked; exit: bar collapses to a single point which becomes the dot that opens the next scene via transition.

prompts.title: La tensión del partido
prompts.prompt:
VERTICAL 9:16 · ~10 s · charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 for Salzburg, slate #8ca6bf for Milan. Lower quarter permanently clear for yellow subtitles.

EDITORIAL VARIANT (0–4.5 s): team reveals with narrative emphasis. First a lime field floods the upper two thirds and 'RED BULL SALZBURG' reveals behind a left-to-right mask in heavy condensed type, with a single warm-white underline swipe; then a slate field replaces it and 'AC MILAN' reveals the same way. Between them, a full-width warm-white rule contracts to the centre and a Spanish narrative word 'TENSIÓN' punches in at scale 1.25→1.0 on the beat. Kinetic, no axes, no sample claims, no invented match events. Entry: mask wipes 0.45 s each; exit via a transition (rule expands into the frame edge) into the statistical variant.

STATISTICAL VARIANT (4.5–10 s): two mirrored horizontal bar pairs on a shared zero origin at the vertical centre, unit 'partidos', shared scale 0–3. Upper pair lime: 'VICTORIAS' {{home.wins}} and 'DERROTAS' {{home.losses}} for Salzburg. Lower pair slate: 'EMPATES' {{away.draws}} and 'DERROTAS' {{away.losses}} for Milan. Bars grow outward from the shared origin in opposite directions with 0.08 s stagger and ease-out cubic; numerals count up in 56 px warm white with the unit 'partidos'. The grounded statistical tension is the contrast between Salzburg's wins and Milan's draws — emphasise the {{home.wins}} bar and the {{away.draws}} bar with a 3 px warm-white outline and a 10 px lift each, joined by a thin bracket captioned in Spanish 'CLAVE DEL PARTIDO'. Supporting context chips appear at the bottom of the chart area in small condensed type: 'Milan · goles a favor' {{away.gf}} and 'Salzburg · arcos en cero' {{home.clean}} — as chips, not axes. A Spanish micro-note in warm white at 55 opacity states 'DATOS HISTÓRICOS · NO SON PRONÓSTICOS' plus the sample: 'Muestra: {{h2h.total}} cruces previos' and 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. Camera: slow 1.0→1.04 push during the emphasis, then locked. Exit: bars retract to origin and the frame fades to charcoal over 0.4 s via transition.
